# [TASK] Self-healing read-through: treat schema-drifted MongoDB documents as cache misses

## Task
Movie documents persisted under an older schema (e.g. `spokenLanguages` as `List<String>` before ADR-010's `List<SpokenLanguage>`) made the read-through path throw a 500 instead of degrading — and kept throwing on every retry, since a failed read never reaches save-through to repair it. Fix: treat an unreadable persisted document as a cache miss.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A document persisted in an outdated shape no longer 500s; a conversion failure is caught, the document is evicted, and the caller re-fetches from TMDB (`MovieServiceTest.getMovieById_WhenPersistedDocumentCannotBeConverted_ShouldEvictAndRefetch`)
- [x] The document is replaced with a current-shape document on next access, not duplicated (`TmdbFacadeIntegrationTest.schemaDriftedDocumentIsHealedOnRead`, `.healedDocumentIsServedLocallyAfterwards`)
- [x] Only mapping/conversion failures are absorbed; a genuine `DataAccessException` still propagates and nothing is deleted (`MovieServiceTest.getMovieById_WhenMongoIsUnavailable_ShouldPropagateAndNotEvict`, `.getMovieById_WhenEvictionFails_ShouldStillReturnFreshlyFetchedMovie`)
- [x] Unit and Testcontainers-integration coverage both exist (`MovieServiceTest`: 3 tests; `TmdbFacadeIntegrationTest.plantedLegacyShapeIsGenuinelyUnconvertible`, `.schemaDriftedDocumentIsHealedOnRead`, `.healedDocumentIsServedLocallyAfterwards`)
- [x] [ADR-011](../blob/main/docs/architecture/adr/011-self-healing-read-through-on-schema-drift.md) documents the decision (manual: verified live through the gateway and the Postman/newman collection)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 7

## Notes
Scoped to movie-service only — actor-service and user-service are PostgreSQL with Flyway/`ddl-auto: validate`, which already catches drift at startup, so the same pattern there would be dead code. This pattern only applies to re-derivable (TMDB-sourced) data; user-owned data must never adopt it, since it can't be re-fetched from anywhere.
